advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the ORDER BY refusal only matches a real trailing ORDER BY clause, not the substring inside a quoted JQL value.
evidence: "if _ORDER_BY_RE.search(jql):" matches anywhere in the string, including inside a quoted literal, not only a trailing clause
The two base queries today (jql_active uncapped, jql_done_recent capped) do not embed such literals, so this is latent rather than currently triggered
advisory.finding: collect_partitioned's ORDER BY refusal uses a case-insensitive regex \border\s+by\b that scans the ENTIRE jql string, so a legitimate exhaustive query containing the substring 'order by' inside a quoted field value (e.g. a summary/text filter) would be refused with ValueError even though it has no real ORDER BY clause.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Verify the unbounded-above (future) window walk-forward does not issue avoidable empty ACLI calls past _now().
evidence: src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/fetch_paging.py:311: if lo is not None:  # unbounded above — walk the upper edge forward
src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/fetch_paging.py:315: return _now(), span  # the root: everything created so far, and everything after
Ticket implementation comment: 'the drain settles at roughly six windows ... about 100 ACLI calls where today's (failing) query makes 14'
advisory.finding: In _split_window, when the root window [None, None) is split, the right child [mid, None) walks its upper edge FORWARD via `lo + span` (line 312), which can generate windows extending past _now() into the future. Such windows always match zero issues (nothing is created in the future) yet each still costs a live ACLI call, adding futile probes on top of the disclosed ~100-call amplification.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Strengthen test_no_slice_is_ever_served_more_than_the_ceiling to assert that every COMPLETED (unsplit) window stays under the ceiling, not merely that one such window exists.
evidence: docstring: "Every window handed to the pager stays under the ceiling — capacity is bounded by the WINDOW"
completed = [j for j in client.jqls if len(client._matching(j)) < fetch_paging._ACLI_CEILING]
assert completed, "no window completed under the ceiling"
ABSENCE: no assertion that all completed leaf windows (windows the drain did NOT further split) are under the ceiling; only existence of one such window is checked.
advisory.finding: test_no_slice_is_ever_served_more_than_the_ceiling under-asserts: its name/docstring claim 'every window handed to the pager stays under the ceiling', but the only assertion (`assert completed`) merely checks that at least ONE served window fell under the ceiling. A regression that served some window at or over the ceiling would still pass as long as any single window is under it, so the test does not detect the behavior it names.
scenarios: A bisection bug that stops splitting a still-over-ceiling window would leave an over-ceiling completed window, yet this test stays green because other windows complete under the ceiling.
advisory.suggested_fix: Assert on the leaf windows the drain accepted as complete: e.g. compute leaves = [j for j in client.jqls if len(client._matching(j)) < _ACLI_CEILING] AND assert that no jql in client.jqls that was NOT further split has _matching >= _ACLI_CEILING — i.e. assert all(len(client._matching(j)) < fetch_paging._ACLI_CEILING for j in <leaf windows>).
